operators.name: linear_forward
semantics: Performs linear transformation: output = input @ weight.T + bias (if bias is not None).
Corresponds to reference self.fc(x) which is nn.Linear without activation.
Uses cuBLAS/cuDNN if possible, but in this contract we define the interface; implementation in .cu/.cpp.
Input shape [N, in_features], weight shape [out_features, in_features], output shape [N, out_features].
Bias is optional and can be None; if provided, it is broadcast across N dimension.
Supports non-contiguous input? For simplicity, we assume contiguous input in implementation but contract allows strides.

operators.name: gelu_forward
semantics: Applies Gaussian Error Linear Unit (GELU) element-wise: output = input * 0.5 * (1 + erf(input / sqrt(2))).
Corresponds to F.gelu(x) with default approximate='none'.
Input and output have same shape and dtype.

operators.name: gt_forward
semantics: Performs element-wise greater-than comparison: output = input > threshold.
The threshold is a scalar float; in reference it is a tensor but we pass scalar for efficiency.
Output is boolean tensor with same shape as input.
If threshold not provided, default is 0.5 as in reference.

operators.name: add_forward
semantics: Performs broadcasting addition: output = input (bool) + other (float).
Boolean input is converted to float for addition, resulting in float32 output.
Broadcasting follows PyTorch semantics: input shape [batch_size, in_features] and other shape [in_features, 1, 1] produce output shape [in_features, batch_size, in_features].
The output layout is not contiguous; it is a broadcasted view with stride [batch_size*in_features, in_features, 1] as per reference.
The addition is implemented as a custom kernel that computes the broadcasted result without materializing the full intermediate if possible, but for this contract we just define the op.
Input boolean tensor is treated as 0/1 when cast to float.
Linear transformation: y = x @ fc.weight.T + fc.bias.
Result stored as CUDA float32 tensor.
Element-wise GELU activation (exact formula with erf).
Same shape and dtype as input.
Creates a CPU float32 scalar tensor with value 0.5.
Shape [] (scalar).
Element-wise comparison x > 0.5, producing boolean tensor.
Threshold is a scalar tensor on CPU; comparison is done on CUDA, so threshold is implicitly transferred.
Output shape [128, 1536], dtype bool.
Broadcasting addition between boolean tensor shape [128, 1536] and float bias shape [1536, 1, 1].
Boolean is cast to float (0 or 1) before addition.
Output shape [1536, 128, 1536], dtype float32.
The output is non-contiguous due to broadcasting; its stride is [196608, 1536, 1].
Returns the final tensor of shape [1536, 128, 1536].
